body:
## Context
ADR-025 scheduled the OKR-items successor at DESIGN-023 phase F. Locked User Decisions 4 and 8 place goal records and metric derivation in the generic kernel, while §5.4 retains the skill's measurement and approval responsibilities. Work-store activation in ADR-026 is prior authority for the already-native work lane, not evidence of goals approval.

## Options
Keep legacy structured goals/decide writers, or move their structured facts to the native process template with owned narrative attachments. The former retains two state systems; the latter follows the locked plan and preserves version-scoped identity and honest unknowns.

## Chosen
This successor supersedes ADR-017 and ADR-022 at reviewed activation, as ADR-025 scheduled; it amends the storage medium/authoring boundaries of ADR-015 and ADR-019 while retaining one-home-per-fact. Root/H owns the remaining ADR-011/012/014 dispositions and narrative reconciliation. At reviewed activation, apply the F process template and append reconciled objective/KR/check/phase/design/ADR items. Preserve all existing work items, IDs and events. Preserve exact legacy labels, source scopes, source hashes, attachments and metadata including superseded/archived ADRs. Do not infer measured currents from prose. Kernel-derived metric shape does not prove criteria, command execution or user approval.

## Consequences
The skill runs input/meaning/measurement checks and records actual consent. Narratives remain lane-owned attachments; legacy structured headers/stores and journals are frozen history. Old writer tests receive explicit H dispositions. Sparse filename ceilings need an approved generic primitive; placeholders and direct SQLite/event edits are forbidden. No phase replanning, remote publication, V4 self-review or H/V5 sign-off is implied.

## Evidence
Root inserts the exact integrated commit, reviewed migration/replay/source-parity receipts, architecture start/delivery/freshness paths, actual prefix ceilings, fresh backups and activation consent reference before acceptance.
